scope: Proposition 5.1 (One amplification block) of the manuscript “Quantitative lower bounds for trace reconstruction” (preprints/quantitative-lower-bounds-for-trace-reconstruction-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 122 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6b28f84fe939dfe5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the parameters of Section 2, let 1 ≤ i ≤ D and suppose a level-(i − 1) pair satisfies Definition 2.2 with constants C, ω, MB. Set C′ = max{C, Cabs/ω}. The input pair remains valid when C is replaced by C′, and there exists a level-i pair satisfying the definition with the same constants C′, ω, MB, with di = di−1 + (bi − 1)/4 − .05, Ei ≤ ∆ + (ℓi/ℓi−1)Ei−1. Every preceding level constructed with C also remains valid with C′, and this enlarged value is retained in later blocks. The conclusion is uniform over all levels along the stated joint asymptotic regime.
